Name: ManyClasses 1
Description: First study of the ManyClasses model (Fyfe et al. 2021, AMPPS; 48 authors): the same experiment - immediate vs delayed feedback on class assignments - embedded in 38 authentic college classes across institutions, topics, and student populations. Overall effect of feedback timing was 0.002 (95% HDI [-0.05, 0.05]): no generalizable effect, and none of 40 preregistered moderators was credibly nonzero. A test of whether a widely recommended, lab-supported practice generalizes to real classrooms.

Name: Special Education Research Accelerator (SERA)
Description: Crowdsourced replication platform for special education research at the University of Virginia (PIs Bryan Cook, Bill Therrien, Vivian Wong), funded by an IES/NCSER methods grant (2019). Uses a standing network of research partner labs and the Causal Replication Framework (Steiner, Wong & Anglin 2019). Pilot (2020/21) crowdsourced a conceptual replication of a 1994 study of teaching methods for science-fact acquisition in elementary students with high-functioning autism across 23 research partners in all nine US Census regions. Pilot results/publication not located during this search (follow up). See also https://www.edreplication.org/replication-studies/sera and IES blog: https://ies.ed.gov/blogs/research/post/developing-and-piloting-the-special-education-research-accelerator

Name: IES Systematic Replication Grants Program (84.305R / 84.324R)
Description: Since FY2019/2020 the Institute of Education Sciences has run dedicated Systematic Replication grant competitions in education (84.305R, NCER) and special education (84.324R, NCSER), funding replications of interventions with prior WWC-standards causal evidence. Known awards: interleaved mathematics practice (R305R220012), SRSD writing effectiveness replication (R305R220020), Sound Partners with peer tutors (R305R220024), national self-affirmation replication (R305R220018); ROOTS kindergarten math replication (R324R200005, U Oregon), ECRI effectiveness replication (R324R210009, RAND), BEST in CLASS (R324R210005), Conjoint Behavioral Consultation (R324R210013), CARE for special educators (R324R210020). Special-ed program page: https://ies.ed.gov/funding/research/programs/research-grants-focused-on-systematic-replication-in-special-education . Published replication results so far include ROOTS (Clarke et al. 2022, null: g -0.09 to 0.12 vs original 0.30-0.38) and ECRI (Fien et al. 2021, positive); most grants still in progress - no aggregate replication rate published.

Name: EEF efficacy-to-effectiveness re-trials
Description: The Education Endowment Foundation systematically re-tests interventions that showed promise in efficacy RCTs with larger effectiveness RCTs under everyday, scalable delivery conditions - a de facto replication programme. Re-trials identified in this search (16 with reported results): positive results NOT retained at scale for Philosophy for Children (+2m to 0), Catch Up Literacy (+2m to 0), Catch Up Numeracy (+ to 0/negative for FSM), Switch-on Reading (+3m to 0), Accelerated Reader (+3m to 0), Thinking Doing Talking Science (+3m to 0), Changing Mindsets (to 0), ReflectED (+ to -1m), Improving Working Memory (+3m to 0), with IPEELL mixed (+9m to small +, negative spillovers) and Mathematical Reasoning reduced (+1m); positive results broadly retained for 1stClass@Number (+2m), Maths Champions (+3m), ABRA (+2m), Tutor Trust (+3m), NELI (positive in re-grant RCT and +4m language in scale-up FRD evaluation). No official aggregate replication rate published by EEF; counts above reflect this (near-complete but unofficial) enumeration. EEF's own synthesis page (Info URL) was 403-blocked during this search - verify against it.

Name: 3ie Replication Programme / Replication Paper Series (education-related subset)
Description: The International Initiative for Impact Evaluation (3ie) funded ~23 internal replications of influential development impact evaluations across four rounds, published via its Replication Paper Series (RPS) and journals. Education-related replications identified: (1) the two-part re-analysis of Miguel & Kremer's (2004) Kenya school-based deworming trial (Aiken et al. 2015 pure replication, 10.1093/ije/dyv127; Davey et al. 2015 statistical replication, 10.1093/ije/dyv128 - both IJE), which weakened evidence for the school-attendance externality claims; and (2) RPS21 (Reimao 2019) replicating Baird, McIntosh & Ozler's (2011) 'Cash or Condition?' Malawi cash-transfer experiment on schoolgirls' schooling outcomes. RPS papers 1-16 could not be fully enumerated (site pagination is JS-based) - a few additional education-related entries may exist.

Name: Investing in Innovation (i3) / EIR scale-up evaluations
Description: The US Department of Education's i3 (later EIR) program required independent evaluations when previously-validated interventions were scaled, effectively re-testing earlier efficacy findings. Flagship example: Reading Recovery i3 scale-up (May et al.) - Year-1 multisite RCT effect of 0.69 SD on ITBS Total Reading (AERJ 2015, 10.3102/0002831214565788) and confirmatory 4-year report (CPRE 2016), but a long-term regression-discontinuity follow-up found significantly NEGATIVE effects of -0.19 to -0.43 SD on 3rd/4th-grade reading tests (May et al. 2023, JREE, 10.1080/19345747.2023.2209092). Other large i3 scale-up evaluations (Success for All, KIPP, Teach For America) were not verified during this search - follow up before adding.

Name: Cook et al. 2024 special education replication corpus ("Same as It Ever Was")
Description: Not a coordinated initiative but a coded corpus: Cook, Therrien et al. (Remedial and Special Education, 2024) catalogued every self-labelled replication in the 44 JCR special-education journals 2015-2022 (update of Makel et al. 2016). Per-study coded data on OSF. Author-stated outcomes: 58 success, 7 mixed, 6 failure, 7 unclear (74.4% success of 78; success rates of self-labelled replications are inflated by author overlap and publication bias).

Name: Hao et al. 2019 computing education replication corpus
Description: Not a coordinated initiative but a coded corpus: Hao et al. (ACM TOCE, 2019; ITiCSE working group) catalogued all replication studies in computing education research 2009-2018. Full per-study dataset on GitHub. Reported outcomes: 34 success, 16 mixed/partial, 4 failure (63% success of 54).
